import graph from '@site/data/protocol-graphs/software-change-1.json';

Deliver a change to a software system: implement it, verify the current implementation revision, merge it under authority, release and deploy it, and accept it once its objective is realized; or close it declined, superseded or abandoned on an explicit decision, or rolled back on a complete rollback result. A case fixes its risk, which selects the obligations that apply, and its change kind, which selects whether a regression must be reproduced before the implementation is edited.

- **Id:** `software.change`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Source:** [`protocols/software-change/1.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/engineering-protocols/blob/main/protocols/software-change/1.yaml)

## Dependency graph

Which actions may produce which evidence, which claims that evidence establishes, and which outcomes and obligations rest on those claims. Hover or focus a node to trace what it rests on.

<ProtocolGraph data={graph} />

## Actions

What can be done in a case: what it needs first, which authority it requires, the class of effect it has and the evidence it may produce.

| Action | Description | Precondition | Requires capability | Effect | May produce |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `implementation.edit` | change the implementation in the repository's working revision; a bugfix needs its regression reproduced first | any of (`regression.reproduced` is **TRUE**; input `change_kind` is one of `feature`, `refactor`) | *no authority* | `write` | *no evidence* |
| `release.rollback` | return to a previous release; needs authority to roll back, and invoking it earns no outcome until a rollback result says it is complete | *none* | `release.rollback` | `write` | `rollback_result` |
| `repository.inspect` | read the repository | *none* | *no authority* | `read` | *no evidence* |
| `repository.merge` | merge a revision into the repository's mainline; needs the current implementation revision verified and authority to merge, never only a connection to the repository host | `implementation.verified` is **TRUE** | `repository.merge` | `write` | *no evidence* |
| `tests.run` | run the tests against an implementation revision | *none* | *no authority* | `read` | `test_result` |
| `tests.write` | change the tests in the repository's working revision | *none* | *no authority* | `write` | *no evidence* |

## Evidence kinds

The kinds of evidence this protocol admits.

| Evidence kind | Description | Produced by | Used by claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build_provenance` | the record of how a release was built from an implementation | *no action* | `release.proven` |
| `code_review` | a review of an implementation revision; its result is approved or rejected | *no action* | `implementation.reviewed` |
| `objective_observation` | an observation of whether the intent's objective is met; its result is satisfied or unsatisfied | *no action* | `objective.realized` |
| `operational_observation` | an observation of the running system; its result is healthy or unhealthy | *no action* | `deployment.healthy` |
| `rollback_result` | the result of returning a release to the one before it; its result is complete or partial | `release.rollback` | *no claim* |
| `test_result` | the result of running tests against an implementation revision; its result is pass or fail | `tests.run` | `implementation.verified`, `regression.reproduced`, `tests.pass` |

## Claims

Each claim is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN, established from evidence by its predicate. Missing or stale evidence leaves a claim UNKNOWN, never FALSE.

| Claim | Description | True when |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment.healthy` | the deployment is running healthily | evidence `operational_observation` with result `healthy` about `deployment` |
| `implementation.reviewed` | the current implementation revision is reviewed | evidence `code_review` with result `approved` about `implementation` |
| `implementation.verified` | the current implementation revision is verified | all of (evidence `test_result` with result `pass` about `implementation`) |
| `objective.realized` | the intent's objective is met | evidence `objective_observation` with result `satisfied` about `intent` |
| `regression.reproduced` | a test has failed, reproducing the regression a bugfix repairs; the match names no subject | evidence `test_result` with result `fail` |
| `release.proven` | the current implementation revision is verified and the current release revision carries build provenance; nothing here ties that release to the verified implementation revision | all of (`implementation.verified` is **TRUE**; evidence `build_provenance` about `release`) |
| `tests.pass` | the tests pass for the current implementation revision | evidence `test_result` with result `pass` about `implementation` |

## Obligations

What must be done before a case can be complete, and what discharges it. An obligation stays open until its predicate is TRUE; its predicate being UNKNOWN does not discharge it.

| Obligation | Description | Applies when | Discharged when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `health.required` | the deployment is healthy; applies at critical risk | input `risk` is one of `critical` | `deployment.healthy` is **TRUE** |
| `provenance.required` | the release is proven; applies at elevated risk and above | input `risk` is one of `critical`, `elevated` | `release.proven` is **TRUE** |
| `review.required` | the current implementation revision is reviewed; applies at standard risk and above | input `risk` is one of `critical`, `elevated`, `standard` | `implementation.reviewed` is **TRUE** |
| `tests.required` | the tests pass for the current implementation revision; applies at every risk | input `risk` is one of `critical`, `elevated`, `standard`, `trivial` | `tests.pass` is **TRUE** |

## Outcomes

The legitimate terminal interpretations of a case, and what each requires.

| Outcome | Description | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `abandoned` | the case closed because the change was explicitly abandoned without reaching any planned outcome | decision `explicitly_abandoned` |
| `accepted` | the case closed with its result accepted; needs the release proven, the deployment healthy and the objective realized | all of (`deployment.healthy` is **TRUE**; `objective.realized` is **TRUE**; `release.proven` is **TRUE**) |
| `declined` | the case closed because the change was explicitly declined; needs no implementation | decision `explicitly_declined` |
| `rolled_back` | the case closed with its release rolled back; needs a rollback result about the current release revision that says the rollback is complete | evidence `rollback_result` with result `complete` about `release` |
| `superseded` | the case closed because another change explicitly superseded it | decision `explicitly_superseded` |

## Artifacts

The things whose revisions evidence is bound to.

| Artifact | Description |
|---|---|
| `deployment` | a release running in an environment |
| `implementation` | a revision of the code that realizes the plan |
| `intent` | what the change is meant to achieve |
| `plan` | the intended steps toward the intent |
| `release` | a versioned, deployable unit of the system |
| `system_specification` | the specified behaviour of the system concerned |

## Case inputs

What a case fixes when it opens: each input takes one of the values listed, and is never UNKNOWN.

| Input | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `change_kind` | what the change is; a bugfix must reproduce its regression with a failing test before the implementation is edited | `bugfix`, `feature`, `refactor` |
| `risk` | how much proof the change must carry; each level applies every obligation of the level below it and one more | `critical`, `elevated`, `standard`, `trivial` |
